Two controlled loops, one immutable evidence trail

The interviewer discovers and freezes an eligible belief. The persuader selects only reason-relevant evidence, blocks unsupported claims, and records immediate and seven-day outcomes.

How to present this diagram

Begin at the top-left and follow the five horizontal lanes. Click any component to explain its job, inputs, outputs and failure rule.

Input
A real participant describing a recent consequential decision
Output
A verified intervention and auditable measurement record
Owner
LLM judgment, deterministic rules and human approval are kept separate
Core safety rule: no supporting passage means no delivered claim.
What to say

“The design contains two controlled loops: discovery and persuasion. Each probabilistic model decision is surrounded by a deterministic record or gate, and V1 keeps a human check immediately before delivery.”

Tip: click the highlighted nodes while screen sharing instead of reading every label.

What to build first

01 · prove intakeBelief record + eligibility

Reject unsuitable cases without inventing cost.

02 · bound knowledgeOne-domain evidence library

Exact passages, scope and exclusions.

03 · prove safetyClaim audit + human gate

Store every pass, rewrite and refusal.

04 · test hypothesisPersonalized vs fixed

Control claim and word budgets.

05 · prove outcomeNow + day seven

Measure belief retention and behavior.

Decisions to get from Siddhant

1Is belief discovery evaluated as part of the product?
2Separate participants or both interventions per participant?
3What establishes a qualifying cost and acceptable evidence?
4Is a human approval gate acceptable in the final V1?
5What participant count and delayed outcome are expected?
